plugins.name: quality-supervisor
plugins.description: Agentic QA quality-intelligence for Qase: coverage gaps, failure triage and root-cause, flakiness vs. regression, release-readiness gating, a visual quality pulse for any period, and branch impact analysis with a regression checklist — driven through the Qase MCP server, with Qase as the system of record.

skills.name: analyzing-change-impact
skills.description: Analyze what a feature branch changes and produce a QA-facing impact analysis plus a regression/new checklist, grounded in the project's existing Qase cases. Use when the user asks for an impact analysis, change impact, risk analysis, or blast radius of a branch or PR; what QA should test for these changes; a QA checklist or test plan for a branch; what could break; or which existing tests to re-run before merging. Reads the repository diff and Qase; renders an HTML report.
headings: Step 1: Find the base branch and collect the diff
1. Local: the remote HEAD ref (set by clone / `git remote set-head`)
2. Network fallback: ask the remote directly
Trace transitive callers for shared code
Step 4: Ground regression in existing Qase coverage
Step 5: Requirements, when they are available
Posting to a ticket — only when asked

skills.name: analyzing-test-coverage
skills.description: Find where a Qase project's test coverage is thin. Use when the user asks about test coverage or coverage gaps; what isn't tested, untested areas, or what is missing tests; which cases are still manual, not automated, or yet to be automated; which cases have never been run or executed; which suites are empty, thin, or hold no cases; how much of the project is automated; which cases are stale or outdated; or wants test cases drafted to close a gap.
headings: What "coverage" can and cannot mean here
2. Execution coverage — what has never run
5. Risk weighting — check it is possible first

skills.name: analyzing-test-flakiness
skills.description: Find genuinely flaky tests in a Qase project — cases that both pass and fail — and separate them from tests that are simply broken. Use when the user asks which tests are flaky, unreliable, unstable, intermittent, or non-deterministic; about test stability, flakiness, or the flake rate; which tests pass sometimes and fail other times, or fail randomly; which tests to quarantine, mute, or flag as flaky; or whether a specific test is flaky or a real regression.
headings: 1. Seed context and settle the window
2. Find candidates — cases that failed more than once
3. Get the pass/fail split for those candidates
Confirmed flaky (ranked by fail rate × runs)

skills.name: assessing-release-readiness
skills.description: Produce an evidence-backed go / no-go assessment for a Qase release scope — a milestone, a test plan, or a set of runs. Use when the user asks whether they are ready to ship, release, or cut a version; for a go/no-go, a release sign-off, or a quality gate; what is blocking the release or holding it up; whether a milestone or sprint is done; how a release is tracking; or whether it is safe to deploy.
headings: The failure mode this skill exists to avoid
1. Resolve the scope — by title, never by ID
2. Execution progress — from run stats, and mind `untested`
4. Blocking defects — use REST, not QQL
7. Decide, and be explicit about the bar

skills.name: reporting-quality-pulse
skills.description: Build a visual "Quality Pulse" report card for a Qase project over any period the user chooses — daily, weekly, biweekly, monthly, sprint, or a custom date range. A styled HTML card summarizing test execution, pass rate, defect backlog, case activity, and active users for that window. Use this whenever the user asks for a quality pulse, QA pulse, quality/test report card, test health summary, sprint QA snapshot, release health check, or any "how is testing going" overview for a Qase project over some period, even if they don't say the word "pulse".
headings: Step 5 — Offer to make it recurring

skills.name: triaging-test-failures
skills.description: Triage the failures in a Qase test run: cluster them by error signature, separate real product bugs from automation, environment, and flaky noise, and file defects. Use when the user asks to triage a run; why a run, a build, or the tests in it failed; why last night''s or the latest run failed or is red; what broke; to investigate, group, cluster, or classify failures; which failures are real bugs versus noise; or to file defects for a failed run.
headings: Quality Supervisor — Failure Triage / Root-Cause Analysis
1. Find the run and its real failure count — one query
2. Frame the scale before looking at details
3. Fetch the failing results — via REST, not QQL
4. Cluster by cause, not by symptom
6. File defects — only after approval, and only with honest claims
